title: Garmin Run Marathon Series Philippines 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Garmin Run Philippines Review: 3am Start, Humidity, Cut-off, Field
meta_description: Garmin Run Philippines review: the 2025 half marathon at Filinvest City, a 3am start at 28°C with a 25°C dew point, a 7am cut-off, kit, fees and how fast the field ran.
dek: What running Garmin's Manila half marathon was like in 2025: the 3am start, the humidity, the cut-off, the kit and fees, how fast you need to be to place, and what changes when the race moves to SM Mall of Asia in 2026.
verdict: Enter if you want a big, chip-timed half marathon in Metro Manila with a four-hour limit and do not mind a 3am start. The 2025 race put 3,012 runners through the 21 km, with a 7am cut-off for every distance and a finisher's shirt and medal for the half. The front is modest: tenth place was 1:29:33 for men and 1:58:11 for women, and half the field took longer than 2:45. The catch is the air: at the 3am start Manila's airport recorded 28°C with a 25°C dew point, and no route map was posted on the 2025 registration page. The 2026 race also moves to a new venue, so read the route before you plan your pacing.

sections.heading: Start Times and Cut-off: A 3am Half With Four Hours to Finish
paragraphs: The 2025 race was held on Sunday 26 October at the Filinvest City Events Grounds in Alabang, Muntinlupa, the second Philippine edition of the Garmin Run Asia Series [1][2]. The 21 km started at 3am, with assembly from 2am; the 10 km followed at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5.30am [1].

Every distance closed at 7am [1]. That gave the half marathon four hours, the 10 km two and a half and the 5 km an hour and a half, which is a generous limit for a 21 km. Every bib carried a timing tag [1]. The results list 28 half marathoners with gun times beyond four hours, the slowest in 4:17:19 [3], so the results point to the limit being applied loosely at the finish in 2025. Do not plan on it.
The 2026 race keeps the same shape: the 21 km at 3am, the 10 km at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5am, all with a 7am cut-off [4][5].

sections.heading: The Weather: 28°C and a 25°C Dew Point at 3am
paragraphs: Ninoy Aquino International Airport, about 10 km north of Filinvest City, recorded 28°C at 3am on race morning, with a dew point of 25°C, 84% humidity and a 3-knot wind [6]. The temperature eased to 27°C between 4am and 6am, when humidity peaked at 94%, then rose back to 28°C at the 7am cut-off and 30°C at 8am [6]. No rain was reported [6].

A dew point of 25°C is oppressive for running: the air is so wet that sweat barely evaporates, so you heat up even in the dark. The median 21 km runner crossed the line at about 5.45am [3], so most of the field ran the whole way in near-saturated air with almost no wind. Start slower than your usual half-marathon pace and drink early.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Corsino Satinitigan won the men's 21 km in 1:10:38, ahead of David Kipkoech Kipsang in 1:12:16 and Ritchie Estampador in 1:13:39. Jessa Mae Roda won the women's race in 1:31:45, from Eloisa Cusi in 1:34:10 and Jocelyn Elijiran in 1:40:54 [2][3].

Behind the podium the field thins fast. Tenth place in the 21 km was 1:29:33 for men and 1:58:11 for women, on the gun times the organiser ranks by [3]. Only 267 of the 3,012 finishers broke two hours, two thirds finished inside three hours, and the median chip time was 2:45:09 [3]. The 10 km was won in 33:28 by Welmer Jeck Labrador and in 39:39 by Edna Magtubo, and tenth man ran 39:36 [2][3].

The race is growing. The organiser put the 2025 turnout at a record 7,700 runners, including 238 from more than 20 countries [2]; the results list 3,012 finishers in the 21 km, 2,855 in the 10 km and 983 in the 5 km [3]. The 21 km had 1,843 finishers in 2024 [7]. The results show two start waves for the 21 km and the 10 km [3].

sections.heading: Race Weekend: Kits, Fees and Rules
paragraphs: Race kits were delivered from 22 September for a fee of ₱200 within Metro Manila and ₱400 outside it, or collected in person: in the BGC area from 7 to 13 October and in Alabang from 15 to 25 October, 11am to 8pm [1].

Every entry included a race bib with a timing tag, a tote bag, a finisher's medal and hydration on the course; 21 km runners got an event singlet and a finisher's shirt, the shorter distances an event shirt [1]. Finishers inside the qualifying time also got an e-certificate [2]. After the race a Garmin Village hub had device displays, games and partner booths [2].

Entry for the 21 km cost ₱2,200 at the early-bird rate and ₱2,800 at the last-chance rate, plus a ₱50 web fee; the 10 km went from ₱1,600 early bird to ₱2,200 last chance, and the 5 km from ₱1,400 to ₱2,000 [1]. The 2026 price chart uses the same early-bird, regular and last-chance rates [8].

Entries were not refundable, and the 2025 checkout called them non-transferable [1]. If the race is postponed, the organiser reschedules and gives no refund or credit to anyone who cannot make the new date [1]. That matters in typhoon season: the first Manila race was postponed from 17 November to 1 December 2024 because of an incoming typhoon [9]. For 2026 the organiser's FAQ says entries can be transferred by email before race day, while the Kinetic sales page says they cannot [5][10]; get the answer in writing before you count on it.

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a large, chip-timed half marathon near Manila with four hours to finish and full results for every runner [3]. The limit suits a first 21 km, and the 10 km and 5 km suit newer runners.
Think twice if you are chasing a fast time in cool air, or if you want to know the course before you enter: no route map was posted on the 2025 registration page [1].

The 2026 race is on Sunday 25 October at the SM Mall of Asia Complex in Pasay, a new venue [8][4]. The organiser's sales partner said starting points would be announced later [10], so the route has not been published. Read it, and the race guide the organiser emails a few days before the race [5], before you set a pace.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's registration and results pages, airport weather records and the organiser's press release.

faqs.question: What time does Garmin Run Philippines start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2025 the 21 km started at 3am, the 10 km at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5.30am, all at Filinvest City in Alabang. For the 25 October 2026 race at SM Mall of Asia the organiser lists 3am, 4.30am and 5am, with assembly for the 21 km from 2am.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off at Garmin Run Philippines?
faqs.answer: 7am for every distance. In 2025 that gave the 21 km four hours, the 10 km two and a half hours and the 5 km an hour and a half. The results still list 28 half marathoners who finished after 7am, the slowest in 4:17:19, but do not count on that leeway in 2026.

faqs.question: How humid is Garmin Run Philippines?
faqs.answer: Very. At the 3am start in 2025, Manila's airport recorded 28°C with a 25°C dew point and 84% humidity, and almost no wind. Humidity rose to 94% by 6am, and the temperature was back at 28°C at the 7am cut-off and 30°C by 8am. Pace for the air, not the distance.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at Garmin Run Philippines?
faqs.answer: Not very fast. In the 2025 21 km the winners ran 1:10:38 and 1:31:45, but tenth place was 1:29:33 for men and 1:58:11 for women. Only 267 of 3,012 finishers broke two hours, and the median chip time was 2:45:09. A 1:29 man or a sub-1:58 woman made the top ten.

faqs.question: Can you get a refund or transfer a Garmin Run Philippines entry?
faqs.answer: No refund. Entry fees are non-refundable, and if the race is postponed there is no refund or credit for anyone who cannot make the new date. The 2025 checkout called entries non-transferable. For 2026 the organiser's FAQ allows transfers by email before race day, but a sales partner says otherwise, so confirm first.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous edition (26 October 2025, Filinvest City, Alabang). Start times, cut-off, kit and fees come from the organiser's registration data; field depth from the organiser's full results, ranked by gun time as the organiser does; weather from airport METAR observations, not a forecast. The official Garmin event pages now redirect to Garmin's home page, and no 2025 route map, runner account or Filipino-language race report could be found. The organiser's 7,700 turnout is a registration-style figure; the results list 6,850 finishers across the three distances. Transfer rules for 2026 conflict between the organiser's FAQ and the Kinetic sales page; both are given. No rating.
